title: Including fibrant objects preserves coherent localization
statement:
Use ordinary nerves, quasicategories, equivalences and entire coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing all the categories below. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with terminal object $1$, and let $W,P$ be classes of arrows containing all isomorphisms and closed under composition. Suppose $W$ has two-out-of-three. Call $a$ fibrant when $a\to1$ belongs to $P$, and let $\mathcal A_f$ be the full subcategory of fibrant objects. Assume that for every $p:x\to y$ in $P$ with $x,y$ fibrant, and every $v:y'\to y$ with $y'$ fibrant, the pullback $x'=y'\times_yx$ exists, is fibrant, and $x'\to y'$ belongs to $P$; if $p\in W$, also $x'\to y'\in W$. Assume further that every $f:a\to b$ with fibrant codomain has a factorization $a\xrightarrow{w}a'\xrightarrow{p}b$ with $w\in W$, $p\in P$, and $a'$ fibrant. No functoriality of these factorizations is assumed, and arbitrary objects of $\mathcal A$ need not be fibrant.

Both ordinary nerves have coherent localizations at their specified weak equivalences, and the inclusion induces an equivalence
$$L(\mathcal A_f,W|_{\mathcal A_f})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }L(\mathcal A,W).$$
Here a coherent localization $q:N\mathcal B\to L(\mathcal B,V)$ means that, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction along $q$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L(\mathcal B,V),\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal B,\mathcal E)$ on functors inverting $V$, retaining every coherent transformation and higher simplex.

source.place: Definition 7.4.6, Definition 7.4.12(i)-(ii), Theorem 7.5.18 (first assertion), applied to an ordinary nerve; existence is Definition 7.1.2 and Proposition 7.1.3. Read online 2026-10-17, printed pp. 360-361, 365-366 and 380; localization definition and existence on pp. 323-324. No Stacks tag states this coherent-localization theorem. WANTED: an archived copy in literature/.

proof.text: Enlarge universes once so that $\mathcal A$, its full subcategory, and their localizations are small in the chosen universe. The arrow systems on their nerves contain all equivalences and are closed under composition: the equivalences in an ordinary nerve are precisely the isomorphisms. Apply [lem-coef-system-localization-universal] to obtain $q_f:N\mathcal A_f\to X$ and $q:N\mathcal A\to Y$ with exactly the universal property in the statement. Since $q i$ inverts the restricted system, that same universal property supplies $u:X\to Y$ and $u q_f\simeq q i$. Its full functor-category form supplies the coherent natural equivalence, not just an equality on components.

Every localization with this universal property is essentially surjective. Indeed, for $s:C\to D$ let $D_0\subseteq D$ be the full subcategory of objects equivalent to some $s(c)$, with inclusion $j$. The factor $s_0:C\to D_0$ still inverts the system, so universality extends it to $t:D\to D_0$. The equivalence $jts\simeq s$ lifts to $jt\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$: lift its inverse as well by full faithfulness of restriction along $s$; faithfulness identifies both lifted composites with the identity transformations. Thus every $d$ is equivalent to $j t(d)$ and hence to some $s(c)$. Apply this to $q_f$ and $q$. This argument needs no chosen fibrant-replacement functor.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.18, essential-surjectivity observation; expanded using Definition 7.1.2.

proof.text: The hypotheses are the ordinary-nerve form of Definitions 7.4.6 and 7.4.12: $1$ is fibrant since its identity belongs to $P$; pullbacks and trivial-fibration pullbacks between fibrant objects are exactly the assumed ones; the required factorization has fibrant intermediate object by assumption. For an ordinary pullback $x′=y′\times_yx$ and each $z$, its universal property is $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x′)=\operatorname{Hom}(z,y′)\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(z,y)}\operatorname{Hom}(z,x)$. These Hom sets are the discrete mapping spaces of the nerve, so this is also their homotopy pullback; the same test gives its terminal object. Moreover the source definition only asks that the intermediate factor be fibrant implicitly: $a′\to b\to1$ is in $P$ by composition. Apply [lem-coef-fibrant-localized-comma-final]. It gives, for every $x\in\mathcal A_f$, finality of $(q_f\downarrow q_f(x))\to(q\downarrow q(x))$, with the indicated coherent commuting-triangle data. The codomain is the localization of all of $\mathcal A$, not the ordinary slice $\mathcal A/x$.

Apply [lem-coef-final-square-full-faithfulness] with $A=N\mathcal A_f$, $B=N\mathcal A$, $q=q_f$, $r=q$, and lower functor $u$. Inclusion of a full ordinary subcategory is fully faithful also on nerves: its mapping spaces are discrete Hom sets and those Hom sets agree. Step 2 gives essential surjectivity of the left functor $q_f$. Step 3 gives the criterion's final comma functors; identify the terminal target $u q_f(x)$ with $q(x)$ by the displayed equivalence of the square. Consequently $u$ is fully faithful on every mapping space. This applies the general square criterion, whose hypotheses include no Brown structure and whose proof is the space-valued Kan-extension argument, rather than assuming the desired equivalence of localizations.

Factor each terminal arrow $a\to1$ as $a\xrightarrow{w_a}a^f\to1$. Its intermediate object is fibrant and $w_a\in W$, so $q(a)\simeq q(a^f)\simeq u q_f(a^f)$. Every object of $Y$ is equivalent to some $q(a)$ by step 2; hence every object of $Y$ belongs to the full essential image of $u$. Together with step 4, [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] provides a coherent quasi-inverse to $u$ and coherent equivalences of both composites with the identities. This is the asserted equivalence $L(\mathcal A_f,W|_{\mathcal A_f})\simeq L(\mathcal A,W)$. The localizations from step 1 already have the required universal property on all coherent transformations and higher simplices.
